summary: This workflow combines three months of case data, cleans and deduplicates it, then summarizes case counts by month and program for a trend report. It scores 6/10, meaning the migration needs real design decisions rather than a direct rewrite. The main drivers are a Union [5] that matches columns by name, a Formula [6] with multiple date formats and mixed logic, and a Unique [7] step whose result depends on row order.

key_components.description: Three monthly CSV files are read in, one column is renamed [4], and all three are stacked together with the Union [5].
The Formula [6] tool parses dates in several formats, fills in missing member IDs, and standardizes status text.
The Unique [7] tool removes duplicate cases, keeping only the first row seen for each case ID.
Remaining cases are counted by month and program, sorted, and written out as the final trend report.

risks.title: Unique keeps 'first' row, but SQL has no inherent row order
risks.detail: Unique [7] keeps the first row per case ID based on the order Alteryx processes rows, which SQL does not guarantee. Without an explicit ORDER BY in a ROW_NUMBER() rewrite, Redshift could keep a different row, changing which case details survive.

risks.title: Mixed date formats in one field
risks.detail: The open_date field contains at least three different date formats (e.g. slashes, dashes with month names, year-first), handled in Alteryx with nested conditions. Redshift's date functions are stricter about format, so each format must be tested separately to avoid silent parsing errors or nulls.

risks.title: Union relies on matching column names, not position
risks.detail: Union [5] combines sources by matching column names, and one source renames a column beforehand [4]. Redshift's UNION ALL matches by column position, so columns must be listed in the same order in every SELECT or data will land in the wrong column.

risks.title: Blank vs. NULL handling in member ID
risks.detail: The Formula [6] treats empty text and NULL member IDs the same way, but SQL distinguishes them. The rewrite needs to explicitly check for both cases or some 'UNKNOWN' labels could be missed.

risks.title: Text case normalization may differ
risks.detail: Status text is capitalized using TitleCase; Redshift's INITCAP can produce different results for certain words (e.g. hyphenated or apostrophe-containing text), so output should be spot-checked.

risks.title: CSV inputs carry no data types
risks.detail: Source files are plain CSVs with no enforced column types, so the Redshift table definition must explicitly set correct types during COPY load.

next_steps: Confirm the exact set of date formats present in open_date across all three months before writing the TO_DATE logic.
Define the ORDER BY rule that determines which row should be kept as 'first' when deduplicating case_id in the ROW_NUMBER() rewrite.
Align column order and names across all three input sources before converting the Union to UNION ALL.
Decide whether empty-string and NULL member_id values should both map to 'UNKNOWN' and encode that explicitly.
Spot-check INITCAP output against the original TitleCase results for status values.
Define target table schema and data types for the Redshift COPY load of the CSV inputs.
